fork:mht-cet-2023:1.explanation: Pyrrole, piperidine and pyridine each contain nitrogen in the ring. Pyran has five carbon atoms and one oxygen atom in its six-membered ring. It is the nitrogen-free choice.

fork:mht-cet-2023:2.explanation: A body-centred cubic cell contains 8 × ⅛ + 1 = 2 atoms. The cell mass is 2M/Nₐ, so its volume is 2M/(ρNₐ). Reading the printed decimal as 4.8 × 10²⁴, this gives 112/(4.8 × 10²⁴) = 2.33 × 10⁻²³ cm³.

fork:mht-cet-2023:3.explanation: The M shell has principal quantum number n = 3, so it contains the 3s, 3p and 3d subshells. Together these provide 1 + 3 + 5 = 9 orbitals. Two electrons per orbital give a capacity of 18.

fork:mht-cet-2023:4.explanation: Cadmium is oxidized on the left and Cu²⁺ is reduced on the right. For the cell reaction the quotient is [Cd²⁺]/[Cu²⁺] in the concentration approximation; the solid metals contribute unity. Two electrons are transferred, giving E = E° − (0.0592/2) log₁₀ Q at 25 °C.

fork:mht-cet-2023:5.explanation: High temperature favors radical substitution at the allylic position of propene. Replacing one H of CH₃–CH=CH₂ with Br gives BrCH₂–CH=CH₂, or 3-bromopropene.

fork:mht-cet-2023:6.explanation: The S₈ molecule is a puckered eight-membered ring. Each sulfur is bonded to two neighboring S atoms and has two lone pairs. Its measured S–S–S angle is about 108°, for which 107° is the listed value.

fork:mht-cet-2023:7.explanation: A Lewis acid–base bond forms when one partner supplies both bonding electrons. The electron-pair donor is the Lewis base, so its defining action is to donate an electron pair.

fork:mht-cet-2023:8.explanation: A negatively charged sol is coagulated by counterions, which are positively charged here. The Hardy–Schulze rule gives greater coagulating power to the counterion of greater charge. Al³⁺ therefore outranks Ba²⁺.

fork:mht-cet-2023:9.explanation: Melting takes 7000 J per mole from the surroundings. For a thermal reservoir at 300 K, its entropy change is qₛᵤᵣᵣ/T = −7000/300 = −23.3 J K⁻¹ for one mole melted.

fork:mht-cet-2023:10.explanation: Read the two monomers in the diagram. The four-carbon diene is 1,3-butadiene, while the vinyl group attached to CN identifies acrylonitrile. Addition copolymerization of butadiene with acrylonitrile produces nitrile rubber, also called Buna-N.

fork:mht-cet-2023:11.explanation: The longest chain containing the double bond has six carbons. Its double bond begins at carbon 3 from either end. Numbering from the right then gives the alphabetically earlier bromo substituent locant 3 and methyl locant 4, producing 3-bromo-4-methylhex-3-ene.

fork:mht-cet-2023:12.explanation: For the stated fully dissociating dibasic acid, each formula unit supplies two H⁺ ions. The hydrogen-ion concentration is therefore 2 × 0.01 = 0.020 M, and pH = −log₁₀(0.020) ≈ 1.70.

fork:mht-cet-2023:13.explanation: Sc³⁺ loses both 4s electrons and its single 3d electron. With a 3d⁰ configuration it cannot undergo a d–d transition. The other listed ions have partially filled d shells, so Sc³⁺ is the colourless choice here.

fork:mht-cet-2023:14.explanation: The ideal-gas relation gives T = PV/(nR) = (4.926 × 20)/(2 × 0.0821) = 600 K. Subtracting approximately 273 converts this to 327 °C.

fork:mht-cet-2023:15.explanation: Phosphorus has five P–Cl bonds and no lone pair in molecular PCl₅. Five electron domains arrange as three equatorial bonds and two axial bonds, giving trigonal-bipyramidal geometry.

fork:mht-cet-2023:16.explanation: An oxalate ligand attaches through two oxygen donors. Three oxalates thus make six metal–donor bonds to Fe. The coordination number counts these donor atoms and is 6.

fork:mht-cet-2023:18.explanation: Six nitro ligands, NO₂⁻ bonded through nitrogen, contribute −6. Co(III) contributes +3, so the complex has charge −3 and requires three Na⁺ ions. Its formula is Na₃[Co(NO₂)₆].

fork:mht-cet-2023:19.explanation: A straight-chain primary amine can form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds and has a relatively large surface for dispersion interactions. Branching lowers the boiling point relative to n-butylamine, and the tertiary isomer lacks an N–H donor. The highest of the listed isomers is n-butylamine.

fork:mht-cet-2023:20.explanation: Sulfur can form rings and chains of many different sizes and also has different crystalline modifications. This extensive allotropy makes sulfur the choice among the listed group-16 elements.

fork:mht-cet-2023:21.explanation: Dihydric phenols have two hydroxyl groups on the benzene ring. Catechol is benzene-1,2-diol and quinol is benzene-1,4-diol. Pyrogallol and phloroglucinol each have three hydroxyl groups.

fork:mht-cet-2023:22.explanation: Using 22.4 dm³ per mole at the STP assumed in the options, 2.24 dm³ is 0.10 mol of NH₃. Each molecule contains four atoms. The total is 0.40 × 6.022 × 10²³ = 2.4088 × 10²³ atoms.

fork:mht-cet-2023:23.explanation: Isobutane is (CH₃)₃CH. Its central carbon is bonded to three other carbons and is the only tertiary carbon in each molecule. Thus one mole of isobutane contains one mole of tertiary carbon atoms.

fork:mht-cet-2023:24.explanation: In carbinol nomenclature, names describe the groups attached to the carbon carrying OH. In CH₃–CH(OH)–CH₃, that carbon has two methyl substituents, hence dimethyl carbinol.

fork:mht-cet-2023:25.explanation: The vapour-pressure decrease is 640 − 590 = 50 mmHg. Divide by the vapour pressure of pure benzene at the same temperature to obtain the relative lowering, 50/640 = 0.078125.

fork:mht-cet-2023:26.explanation: A voltaic cell uses a spontaneous redox reaction to produce electrical energy. Oxidation occurs at its negative anode and reduction at its positive cathode. Converting electricity into stored chemical energy describes electrolysis, so C is false for a voltaic cell.

fork:mht-cet-2023:27.explanation: Atom economy is the stoichiometric mass of desired product divided by total stoichiometric reactant mass, multiplied by 100. The figures give 175/225 × 100 = 77.78%, closest to 77.7%.

fork:mht-cet-2023:29.explanation: For a monobasic weak base with concentration C and fractional dissociation α, Kᵦ = Cα²/(1−α). Substitution gives 0.001 × 0.02²/0.98 ≈ 4.08 × 10⁻⁷, or 4 × 10⁻⁷ to the precision of the options.

fork:mht-cet-2023:30.explanation: The measured order with respect to a species is the exponent on its concentration in the rate law. Using first order for CHCl₃ and half order for Cl₂ gives rate = k[CHCl₃][Cl₂]¹ᐟ².

fork:mht-cet-2023:31.explanation: Zero order in B makes the rate independent of its concentration. First order in A gives rate = k[A], so k = 6 × 10⁻⁴ / 0.3 = 2 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹.

fork:mht-cet-2023:32.explanation: At infinite dilution, ionic conductivities add. Subtracting Λ(BaCl₂) from Λ(Ba(OH)₂) exchanges two chlorides for two hydroxides. Add half that difference to Λ(NH₄Cl) to get 129 + (520−280)/2 = 249 Ω⁻¹ cm² mol⁻¹.

fork:mht-cet-2023:33.explanation: For a one-electron ion the Bohr orbital radius is a₀n²/Z. He⁺ has Z = 2, so n = 3 gives 52.9 × 9/2 = 238.05 pm, approximately 238.1 pm.

fork:mht-cet-2023:34.explanation: The solute amount is 4/126 mol and 80 mL of water is approximately 0.080 kg. The molality is (4/126)/0.080 ≈ 0.397 mol/kg. Taking a nonionizing solute gives ΔT𝒇 = 1.86 × 0.397 ≈ 0.74 K.

fork:mht-cet-2023:35.explanation: A close-packed lattice of N atoms of Y has 2N tetrahedral voids. Filling one third puts 2N/3 atoms of X in the lattice. The smallest whole-number X:Y ratio is therefore 2:3, or X₂Y₃.

fork:mht-cet-2023:36.explanation: The three-dimensional Bravais lattices fall into cubic, tetragonal, orthorhombic, hexagonal, trigonal, monoclinic and triclinic systems. These seven crystal systems encompass the 14 lattice types.

fork:mht-cet-2023:37.explanation: The usual textbook reaction is the decomposition of potassium chlorate, KClO₃, to potassium chloride and oxygen. MnO₂ catalyzes this reaction. The formula “KCl₃” in the archived stem omits the oxygen.

fork:mht-cet-2023:38.explanation: Melamine reacts with formaldehyde to form a hard, heat-resistant cross-linked thermoset. It can be moulded into rigid plates and bowls, explaining its use in plastic dinnerware.

fork:mht-cet-2023:39.explanation: In sucrose the glycosidic bond joins the anomeric carbons of both monosaccharide units. Neither can open to give a free reducing group. Maltose, lactose and glucose retain a reducing end.

fork:mht-cet-2023:40.explanation: Acetylating an OH replaces its hydrogen with COCH₃, a net mass gain of 42 u. The gain of 84 u indicates two OH groups. An open-chain aldotriose, CHO–CHOH–CH₂OH, supplies exactly two.

fork:mht-cet-2023:41.explanation: Strontium is an alkaline-earth metal with two outer s electrons and commonly forms Sr²⁺. The alternatives Li, Na and Rb are alkali metals, each typically forming a +1 ion.

fork:mht-cet-2023:42.explanation: For a first-order reaction, t½ = ln 2/k. Substituting k = 2.772 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹ gives 0.693/0.002772 = 250 s.

fork:mht-cet-2023:43.explanation: The boiling point itself is a property of the liquid. Adding solute produces an elevation in that boiling point, and it is the elevation that is colligative. This distinction identifies B.

fork:mht-cet-2023:44.explanation: The ketone or aldehyde first condenses with hydrazine to form a hydrazone. Heating in strong base leads to loss of nitrogen and replaces the carbonyl oxygen by two hydrogens. This combination of reagents identifies the Wolff–Kishner reduction.

fork:mht-cet-2023:45.explanation: Chromyl chloride reacts at the benzylic methyl group of toluene in the Etard oxidation. Hydrolysis of the chromium intermediate releases the aldehyde, so the methyl group has become –CHO and B is benzaldehyde.

fork:mht-cet-2023:46.explanation: Because the cards are replaced, the queen probability is 4/52 = 1/13 on each independent draw. For zero, one, or two queens the binomial probabilities are (12/13)², 2(1/13)(12/13), and (1/13)². In order they give 144/169, 24/169 and 1/169.

fork:mht-cet-2023:47.explanation: Count zero or one unsolved problem among 50 independent attempts. The sum is (4/5)⁵⁰ + 50(1/5)(4/5)⁴⁹. Factoring (4/5)⁴⁹ leaves (4 + 50)/5 = 54/5.

fork:mht-cet-2023:48.explanation: The left side is exactly the differential of (1 + sin x)(1 + cos y). Its first term comes from differentiating the x factor and its second, negative term from the y factor. The product must therefore be constant.

fork:mht-cet-2023:49.explanation: The antecedent is a conjunction with ¬q as its second term. Whenever that conjunction is true, ¬q must be true, so taking r = ¬q makes the implication true. When the conjunction is false, the implication also holds.

fork:mht-cet-2023:50.explanation: Retain points to the right of x = 3, above y = 2x, and below 4x + 3y = 60. The three boundary intersections are (3,6), (3,16) and (6,12). In the supplied graph their closed triangle is S₂.

fork:mht-cet-2023:51.explanation: Completing the squares gives centre (1,2) and radius √5. For two intersections the perpendicular distance from that centre to x−2y−m = 0 must be strictly below √5. Thus abs(m+3) < 5, or −8 < m < 2. The nine integers −7 through 1 qualify.

fork:mht-cet-2023:52.explanation: Since c is parallel to a×b it is perpendicular to both a and b. Expanding the squared norm of a+b+c gives 1 = 1/3 + 1/2 + 1/6 + 2a·b. Thus a·b = 0, so their angle is π/2.

fork:mht-cet-2023:53.explanation: For f(x) = x³+x−1 the derivative 3x²+1 is positive everywhere. The function crosses zero between 0 and 1 because its signs at the endpoints are opposite. Strict increase rules out another real root.

fork:mht-cet-2023:54.explanation: The angle between b and c gives 10 = 5 × magnitude(c) × cos 60°, hence magnitude(c) = 4. Thus magnitude(b×c) = 5 × 4 × sin 60° = 10√3. The last cross product uses perpendicular vectors, so its magnitude is √3 × 10√3 = 30.

fork:mht-cet-2023:55.explanation: The binomial expansion gives B = (I−adj A)³. Here adj A has rows (2,1) and (0,2), so I−adj A has rows (−1,−1) and (0,−1). Its cube has rows (−1,−3) and (0,−1); the four entries sum to −5.

fork:mht-cet-2023:56.explanation: At A the displacement vectors are (−1,−1,8−x) and (−2,−3,2−x). Requiring their dot product to vanish gives 5+(8−x)(2−x)=0, hence (x−3)(x−7)=0. Both 3 and 7 solve the geometry, and 3 is the only listed value.

fork:mht-cet-2023:58.explanation: Write a = f′(1) and b = f″(2). Differentiation gives f′ = 3x²+2ax+b and f″ = 6x+2a. The defining conditions imply a = 3+2a+b and b = 12+2a, which yield a = −5 and b = 2. Therefore f(2) = 8−20+4+6 = −2.

fork:mht-cet-2023:59.explanation: For a nondegenerate harmonic progression, twice the product of the end terms equals the middle term times their sum. With the sine addition formulas this becomes 2(sin²θ−sin²α) = 2sin²θ cos α. Dividing gives sin²θ = 1+cos α. Therefore cos 2θ = 1−2sin²θ = 1−4cos²(α/2).

fork:mht-cet-2023:60.explanation: Put t = arcsin x, so arccos x = π/2−t. The chain rule gives (1−x²)y″−xy′ = d²y/dt² on the interior of the domain. Differentiating y = t² + (π/2−t)² twice with respect to t gives 4.

fork:mht-cet-2023:61.explanation: Since (1+i)² = 2i, the modulus condition is 2/√(a²+1) = 2/√5. Thus a = 2 as it is positive. Rationalizing gives z = (−2+4i)/5, whose conjugate is (−2−4i)/5.

fork:mht-cet-2023:62.explanation: Since A+B+C = π, the angle in the sine is π/2−B and its sine is cos B. The cosine rule gives b² = a²+c²−2ac cos B. Rearranging yields a²+c²−b².

fork:mht-cet-2023:63.explanation: Set u = sin²x+cos³x. Its derivative is 2sin x cos x−3cos²x sin x = sin 2x(1−1.5 cos x), exactly the numerator. The integral is therefore ∫e⁻ᵘdu = −e⁻ᵘ+C.

fork:mht-cet-2023:64.explanation: On the stated interval, sec x + tan x = tan(π/4+x/2), with the angle inside the principal arctangent range. Hence f′(x) = π/4+x/2. Integrating from 0 to 1 gives f(1) = π/4+1/4.

fork:mht-cet-2023:65.explanation: Put t = sin θ. The denominator becomes (2t+1)(t+3), and its reciprocal is (1/5)[2/(2t+1)−1/(t+3)]. Integration gives one fifth of the logarithm of the absolute ratio (2t+1)/(t+3). With this choice of f and A, f/A equals five times that ratio.

fork:mht-cet-2023:66.explanation: From a+2c = −2b, equality of squared magnitudes gives 1+4+4a·c = 4. The two unit vectors therefore have dot product −1/4. Their cross product has magnitude √(1−1/16) = √15/4.

fork:mht-cet-2023:67.explanation: Use u = cot x, so du = −csc²x dx. After removing csc²x the rest of the integrand equals tan²ᐟ³x = u⁻²ᐟ³. Reverse the limits to integrate from 1/√3 to √3. Evaluating 3u¹ᐟ³ gives 3⁷ᐟ⁶−3⁵ᐟ⁶.

fork:mht-cet-2023:68.explanation: For cos x ≠ 0, multiply both sides by cos x. With s = sin x the equation becomes 1+s = 2(1−s²), or (2s−1)(s+1)=0. The root −1 makes the original expression undefined, so s=1/2 yields π/6 and 5π/6.

fork:mht-cet-2023:69.explanation: The vector triple product reduces the equation to 3b = 3c−a(a·c). Thus b is the component of c perpendicular to a. Its length 1 equals 2 sin θ, giving sin²θ = 1/4, cos²θ = 3/4 and sec²θ = 4/3.

fork:mht-cet-2023:70.explanation: The derivatives are dx/dt = 2t cos t and dy/dt = 2t sin t, so a unit tangent is (cos t,sin t). This is a normal vector to the normal line. Its dot product with the point on the curve is 2, yielding the normal-line equation x cos t + y sin t = 2. Its distance from the origin is 2.

fork:mht-cet-2023:71.explanation: A normal to the required plane must be orthogonal to (1,2,−2) and (3,2,1). Their cross product is (6,−7,−4). At (1,−1,2) the expression 6x−7y−4z equals 5, so the plane is 6x−7y−4z−5 = 0.

fork:mht-cet-2023:72.explanation: Each principal arccosine is at most π. For three of them to sum to 3π, every one must equal π, giving x = −1. Its two odd powers are −1 each, and its even power is +1, for a sum of −1.

fork:mht-cet-2023:73.explanation: The intercept form of the line is x/a+y/b−1=0. Its distance from the origin is p = 1/√(1/a²+1/b²). Squaring and inverting gives the sum as 1/p².

fork:mht-cet-2023:75.explanation: With u = cos x the integral becomes ∫(u²−2)/(2u²−1) du. Split the fraction as 1/2 − (3/2)/(2u²−1). Integration gives u/2 − [3/(4√2)] ln abs[(√2u−1)/(√2u+1)] + C. The coefficients and ratio agree with A.

fork:mht-cet-2023:76.explanation: At x = 0 each product factor is 1, and the product derivative is the sum of their derivatives, 1+2+⋯+n = n(n+1)/2. Differentiating the outer nth power multiplies by n at that point, giving n²(n+1)/2.

fork:mht-cet-2023:77.explanation: Write A = (x,2x). The determinant formula gives triangle area equal to half the absolute value of 12−11x. Its rate of change in magnitude is (11/2) times the magnitude of dx/dt. The speed along y = 2x is √5 times this x-speed, so the specified increase is 11/√5 area units per second.

fork:mht-cet-2023:78.explanation: Rationalize the difference of the outer roots. Its numerator becomes √(1+x⁴)−x², which in turn rationalizes to 1/[√(1+x⁴)+x²]. The full expression is x³ divided by [√(1+x⁴)+x²][√(x²+√(1+x⁴))+√2x]. Dividing the factors by x² and x gives limits 2 and 2√2, so the result is 1/(4√2).

fork:mht-cet-2023:79.explanation: Constant continuous compounding with a six-year doubling time gives amount 200 × 2^(t/6). For t = 33 years, the exponent is 5½, giving 200 × 32√2 = ₹6400√2.

fork:mht-cet-2023:80.explanation: Rewrite the function as 1−1/(1+x²). It equals zero at x = 0, increases continuously with the magnitude of x, and approaches 1 while staying below 1 for every finite x. Thus its range is [0,1).

fork:mht-cet-2023:81.explanation: The given family consists of real linear combinations of exponentials with characteristic roots 1+i and 1−i. The polynomial with those roots is (r−1)²+1 = r²−2r+2, so the differential equation is y″−2y′+2y=0.

fork:mht-cet-2023:82.explanation: Let u = 1+x², so x³ dx = (u−1)du/2. Integration gives (1/3)u³ᐟ²−u¹ᐟ²+C. Thus a = 1/3 and b = −1, giving 3ab = −1.

fork:mht-cet-2023:83.explanation: Using the two specified unit normals and distance 1, the lines are x+y = √2 and −x+y = √2. Their product equation is (y−√2)²−x²=0, which rearranges to x²−y²+2√2y−2=0.

fork:mht-cet-2023:85.explanation: Equal positive direction cosines give a direction proportional to (1,1,1). Write a point on the line as (2+t,−1+t,2+t). Substitution into the plane gives 5+4t=9, so t=1. The displacement vector has length √3.

fork:mht-cet-2023:86.explanation: The direction vectors have cross product (15−4λ, λ−10, 5). Its dot product with the vector (1,2,2) between fixed points on the lines is 5−2λ. Squaring the distance formula gives 3(5−2λ)² = (15−4λ)²+(λ−10)²+25. This simplifies to λ²−16λ+55 = 0, whose roots sum to 16.

fork:mht-cet-2023:87.explanation: The middle angle B is 60° because three angles in arithmetic progression sum to 180°. By the sine rule a/c = sin A/sin C. Expanding the two double-angle sines reduces the expression to 2(sin A cos C + sin C cos A) = 2sin(A+C) = 2sin 120° = √3.

fork:mht-cet-2023:88.explanation: With no boys, choose four of the six girls in 15 ways. With one boy, choose one of four boys and three of six girls in 4 × 20 = 80 ways. Each of the 95 teams has four prospective leaders, giving 380 selections.

fork:mht-cet-2023:89.explanation: The permitted interval is [5,6] because x²−11x+30 = (x−5)(x−6) ≤ 0. The derivative 9(x−1)(x−3) is positive throughout. Thus the maximum is the right-endpoint value f(6) = 648−648+162−40 = 122.

fork:mht-cet-2023:90.explanation: The derivative is (x−1)(x−2)/(x⁴+1). The denominator is always positive, so the derivative is negative precisely when its two linear factors have opposite signs. This occurs for 1 < x < 2.

fork:mht-cet-2023:91.explanation: The favourable probabilities are 2/7, 3/7 and 4/7. Assuming the independent reviews implicit in the question, count the three ways exactly two are favourable and the case all three are favourable. With denominator 343 the numerators are 2×3×3, 2×4×4, 5×3×4 and 2×3×4. They sum to 134.

fork:mht-cet-2023:92.explanation: The inner branches of the parabolas are x = −1+√y and x = 1−√y. They meet at y = 1. Integrating the horizontal width 2−2√y from y = 1/4 to 1 gives [2y−(4/3)y³ᐟ²] between the limits, namely 1/3.

fork:mht-cet-2023:93.explanation: At the same temperature and emissivity, the radiated power is proportional to surface area. If the sphere has radius r, a cube of equal volume has edge (4π/3)¹ᐟ³r. Dividing the areas 4πr² and 6(4π/3)²ᐟ³r² gives the sphere-to-cube ratio (π/6)¹ᐟ³.

fork:mht-cet-2023:95.explanation: Motion perpendicular to the field induces emf Blv and current Blv/R. The magnetic drag on the wire is BIl = B²l²v/R. At terminal speed it balances mg, so v = mgR/(B²l²).

fork:mht-cet-2023:96.explanation: At the Balmer limit the upper hydrogen level tends to infinity and the lower level is n = 2. The wavenumber is R(1/2²−0) = R/4. Multiplying by c gives frequency Rc/4.

fork:mht-cet-2023:97.explanation: A string fixed at both ends has resonances at integer multiples of its fundamental. Since 315 Hz and 420 Hz are successive resonances, their separation is the fundamental, 420−315 = 105 Hz.

fork:mht-cet-2023:98.explanation: The single-loop magnetic moment is M = Iπr². Solve for r and multiply by 2π to get the wire length, 2π√(M/(πI)) = √(4πM/I).

fork:mht-cet-2023:99.explanation: The central bright maximum of single-slit diffraction spans twice the width of an ordinary secondary maximum, and the secondary maxima grow successively dimmer. The bright fringes therefore differ in both width and intensity.

fork:mht-cet-2023:100.explanation: After half a turn the velocity reverses, so the magnitude of its change is 2V. The elapsed time is the semicircle length divided by speed, πr/V. Their ratio gives mean acceleration magnitude 2V²/(πr).

fork:mht-cet-2023:101.explanation: At the highest speed on a level curve, friction supplies the required centripetal force, so v² = μgr. For the same curve, halving the allowed speed makes μ one fourth of its original value.

fork:mht-cet-2023:102.explanation: The balance condition gives Rₗₑ𝒻ₜ/8 = 3/2, so the 3 m wire has resistance 12 Ω. For a uniform wire the length per ohm is 3/12 m, or 0.25 m.

fork:mht-cet-2023:104.explanation: The emitter current is Iᴇ = Iᴄ+Iʙ. With α=Iᴄ/Iᴇ and β=Iᴄ/Iʙ this yields α=β/(1+β) and 1/α = 1+1/β. B has the wrong sign in its denominator and is the incorrect relation.

fork:mht-cet-2023:105.explanation: Tension is greatest at the bottom where the speed reaches ωA. The extra required inward force is mv²/l. With ω²=g/l for a small-amplitude pendulum, T = mg + mg A²/l² = mg[1+(A/l)²].

fork:mht-cet-2023:106.explanation: Put five 2 µF capacitors in parallel to make 10 µF. Connect this group in series with the other two individual 2 µF capacitors. Then 1/C = 1/10+1/2+1/2 = 11/10 in inverse microfarads, so C = 10/11 µF.

fork:mht-cet-2023:107.explanation: Inside the liquid a molecule is surrounded by attractive neighbours. Moving a molecule to the surface removes some of these attractions and requires work. It therefore has a higher potential energy at the surface.

fork:mht-cet-2023:108.explanation: At fixed time the phase 5t−4x changes in magnitude by 4Δx. Set this to π/2 radians for a quarter-cycle difference. The smallest positive separation is Δx = π/8 in the units of x.

fork:mht-cet-2023:109.explanation: For a particle of fixed mass at nonrelativistic speeds, p = √(2mE). The de Broglie relation λ=h/p then gives λ ∝ 1/√E.

fork:mht-cet-2023:110.explanation: In an ideal pure inductor or capacitor, voltage and current are a quarter cycle apart. The power factor cos φ is therefore cos 90° = 0, which means zero average real power.

fork:mht-cet-2023:111.explanation: Enclose the uniformly charged sphere in a Gaussian surface of radius r. Its charge is (4πr³/3)ρ, and the flux is 4πr²E. Equating flux to charge divided by ε₀ gives surface field E = ρr/(3ε₀).

fork:mht-cet-2023:112.explanation: Incident radiation is apportioned between absorption, reflection and transmission, so a+r+t=1. An opaque object has zero transmission; the first two fractions must then sum to one.

fork:mht-cet-2023:113.explanation: With W defined as work done by the system, the first law reads ΔU = Q−W. In an adiabatic process Q = 0, so any work output reduces internal energy by the same amount.

fork:mht-cet-2023:114.explanation: For lenses in air P₁+P₂=10 D in contact. With spacing d, total power is P₁+P₂−dP₁P₂, so 6 = 10−0.25P₁P₂ and the product is 16. The two numbers with sum 10 and product 16 are 8 D and 2 D.

fork:mht-cet-2023:115.explanation: Impedance Z is the ratio of AC voltage to current in phasor notation. Its reciprocal Y = I/V = 1/Z is called admittance and has the unit siemens.

fork:mht-cet-2023:116.explanation: The nth orbit radius scales as n², hence the fourth orbit has radius 16r. Its circumference holds four de Broglie wavelengths: 4λ = 2π(16r). Thus λ = 8πr.

fork:mht-cet-2023:117.explanation: The horizontal component of tension supplies centripetal acceleration: T sin θ = mω²r. The orbit radius is L sin θ, so canceling the sine gives T = mLω².

fork:mht-cet-2023:118.explanation: The rms molecular speed at fixed molecular mass scales as √T with T in kelvin. The starting temperature is about 205 K. Doubling the speed requires 4 × 205 = 820 K, or approximately 547 °C.

fork:mht-cet-2023:121.explanation: At equal masses and composition, all three have the same heat capacity. The thin plate exposes the greatest surface area relative to its volume and loses heat fastest under the same surroundings. It approaches room temperature first.

fork:mht-cet-2023:122.explanation: Forward bias injects electrons and holes into an LED junction. Their radiative recombination emits light, so ordinary LED emission uses forward bias.

fork:mht-cet-2023:123.explanation: The solenoid field is μ₀(N/l)I = 4π×10⁻⁷ × (500/0.4) × 3 = 1.5π×10⁻³ T. The small coil has magnetic moment 10 × 0.4 × π(0.1)² = 0.04π A·m². The axes are perpendicular, giving torque μB = 6×10⁻⁵π² ≈ 6×10⁻⁴ N·m.

fork:mht-cet-2023:125.explanation: For uniform density the mass is 4πR³ρ/3. Substituting it into g=GM/R² cancels two powers of the radius, leaving g = 4πGρR/3.

fork:mht-cet-2023:127.explanation: At release the small-angle pendulum has maximum displacement Lθ and zero velocity. The solution satisfying these initial conditions is the cosine form x(t)=Lθ cos(ωt), with ω = √(g/L).

fork:mht-cet-2023:128.explanation: Assume uniform Earth density and small altitude h compared with R. Then gravity at depth is g₀(1−d/R) and at height is approximately g₀(1−2h/R). Dividing gives (R−d)/(R−2h). The altitude expression is the first-order expansion of the inverse-square law.

fork:mht-cet-2023:129.explanation: The initial flux linkage is NBA = 50 × 0.02 × 0.010 = 0.010 Wb-turn. Moving out of the field reduces it to zero. The average emf magnitude is 0.010/t = 0.1 V, giving t = 0.1 s.

fork:mht-cet-2023:130.explanation: Double-slit maxima occur at transverse distance yₙ = nλL/a for fixed screen distance and slit spacing. Thus d₂/d₁ = (6λ₂)/(8λ₁) = 3λ₂/(4λ₁).

fork:mht-cet-2023:131.explanation: An alternating current in the primary creates changing magnetic flux linking the secondary. Faraday’s law then gives a secondary emf proportional to that flux’s rate of change.

fork:mht-cet-2023:132.explanation: For the same reversible cycle operated in opposite directions, the engine efficiency is W/Qₕ and the refrigerator coefficient of performance is Q𝒸/W. Since Qₕ = Q𝒸+W, the efficiency is W/(Q𝒸+W) = 1/(β+1).

fork:mht-cet-2023:133.explanation: The point is 0.20 m radially beyond a sphere of radius 0.10 m, so its centre distance is 0.30 m. Outside, E=σR²/(ε₀r²) = (1.8×10⁻⁶/ε₀)(0.1/0.3)² = 2×10⁻⁷/ε₀ V/m.

fork:mht-cet-2023:135.explanation: For loops of the same wire type and number of turns, equal central fields require I₁/r₁ = I₂/r₂. The larger loop therefore carries twice the current. Its wire length and resistance are also twice as large, giving V₁/V₂ = 2 × 2 = 4.

fork:mht-cet-2023:136.explanation: The left branch carries 5 A into P and the upper branch carries another 4 A in. The arrows on the right and below carry 3 A and 5 A out, respectively. To balance the 9 A entering, the remaining 1 A must leave P toward Q.

fork:mht-cet-2023:137.explanation: For the same liquid and tube material the capillary rise is inversely proportional to radius. The risen mass equals density times πr²h, hence scales linearly with r. Reducing the radius to r/3 reduces that mass to m/3.

fork:mht-cet-2023:139.explanation: An open pipe has an end correction of approximately 0.6r at each open end. Its effective length is therefore l+1.2r. The fundamental wavelength equals twice that length, giving f = V/[2(l+1.2r)].

fork:mht-cet-2023:140.explanation: For a thin prism, deviation is approximately (nᵣₑₗ−1)A. In air the factor is 1.5−1 = 1/2. In water the relative index is (3/2)/(4/3) = 9/8 and the factor is 1/8. The ratio of deviations is 4:1.

fork:mht-cet-2023:141.explanation: The rod rotates about one end, so its moment of inertia is ml²/3. At the mean position its rotation at speed ω gives kinetic energy Iω²/2 = ml²ω²/6, using l for the rod length.

fork:mht-cet-2023:142.explanation: The orbital current is e v/(2πr) and the field at the loop centre scales as current divided by radius, so B ∝ v/r². In hydrogen's Bohr model v ∝ 1/n and r ∝ n². Together these give B ∝ n⁻⁵.
